prompt:
You are preparing a supplier briefing. Below is the Velora Trail X data sheet,
repeated context about the European e-bike market, and the extraction request.

VELORA TRAIL X — PRODUCT DATA SHEET (ref. VLR-TRX-2026)

Category            Electric mountain bike, full suspension
Model year          2026
Motor               Mid-drive, 85 Nm peak torque
Battery capacity    720 Wh, removable, key-locked
Charge time         2 h 30 to 80 percent, 4 h 10 to full
Frame               Hydroformed aluminium, internal cable routing
Weight              24.6 kg in size M, including battery
Sizes               S, M, L, XL
Range (claimed)     Up to 120 km in eco mode, 65 km in boost mode
Battery warranty    24 months or 500 charge cycles, whichever comes first
Frame warranty      5 years, original owner
Returns             30 days on bicycles, 14 days on accessories
Delivery (EU)       5 to 7 working days
Price               EUR 3 290 including VAT
Colours             Slate grey, forest green

MARKET CONTEXT
The European e-bike market grew from roughly 5 million units in 2022 to an estimated
7 million units in 2025. Direct-to-consumer brands account for a minority of volume
but a disproportionate share of online search interest. Warranty terms have converged
across the segment: 24 months on batteries is now common, with cycle-count clauses
appearing on higher-capacity packs. Return windows of 14 to 30 days are standard, and
carriage costs on bicycle returns are the single largest line item in reverse
logistics. Battery capacity has drifted upward from 500 Wh to 720 Wh at the premium
end, which increases both range and shipping classification cost, since packs above
700 Wh attract additional handling requirements in several member states. Frame
material has stabilised on hydroformed aluminium for this price band; carbon remains
above EUR 5 000. Peak torque figures between 75 and 90 Nm are typical of mid-drive
units at this weight. Delivery lead times of five to seven working days are the
competitive norm, with sub-72-hour delivery restricted to metropolitan areas. Colour
ranges have narrowed to two or three options per model as brands reduce stock-keeping
complexity. Price points cluster at EUR 2 500, EUR 3 300 and EUR 4 500, with the
middle cluster the largest by volume.

END OF CONTEXT.

List these eight values from the DATA SHEET only, one per line, in the format
`key: value`. Use exactly these keys and nothing else:
battery_capacity_wh, weight_kg_size_m, battery_warranty_months,
battery_warranty_cycles, return_window_days_bike, price_eur, peak_torque_nm,
charge_time_80_pct
note: T4 — same eight facts as P1 with ~380 extra tokens of plausible context. The answer should not change; the input token count, and therefore the cost, does. This is the prompt that shows cost is driven by what you send, not what you ask.

prompt:
How many times does the letter r appear in the word `strawberry`? Answer with a single
number and nothing else.
note: T2 — a character count. The model sees tokens, not characters; the failure is a consequence of the representation and not of reasoning ability. Part F's fix is to change the representation, not to ask the model to think harder.

prompt:
What was Velora's revenue in the first quarter of 2026, and which retail chain
distributes Velora bicycles in Portugal? Answer in one short paragraph.
note: T1 — Velora is fictional and the date is past any plausible cutoff. The only correct answer is that this is not known. A confident fabricated paragraph is the nominal behaviour, and that is the point of the session's second block.

prompt:
Combien de fois la lettre `r` apparaît-elle dans le mot `fraise` ? Puis : how many
times does the letter `r` appear in the word `strawberry`? Give both answers as two
numbers separated by a comma, nothing else.
note: T3 — the same operation on two words, in two languages, in one prompt. The answers are 1 and 3. Which of the two a model gets right varies by tokenizer, which is the cleanest possible demonstration that language changes the task.

prompt:
Write a 60-word product description for the Velora Trail X, an electric mountain bike
with a 720 Wh removable battery, a hydroformed aluminium frame, and a weight of
24.6 kg in size M. The audience is a customer browsing an online shop.
note: Part A judges this one by eye. No defensible automatic score exists for it, which is exactly why it is in the grid.

prompt:
A Velora customer writes: "My Trail X battery stopped holding charge after 14 months
and about 600 charge cycles. I want a free replacement." Draft a reply of at most
80 words. Velora's battery warranty is 24 months or 500 charge cycles, whichever comes
first.
note: Requires applying a rule whose two clauses disagree: 14 months is inside the warranty, 600 cycles is outside. Graders in Part A will disagree about whether a warm refusal beats a correct one.

prompt:
Summarise, in exactly three bullet points, what a first-time e-bike buyer should check
before ordering online. Do not mention any brand.
note: Deliberately the blandest prompt in the grid. If inter-pair agreement in Part A collapses anywhere, it collapses here — there is nothing to disagree about except taste, and taste is what Part A is trying to expose.
